ev.q: During 2014, 12.7% of workers aged 18–64 years were uninsured (21% decline from 2013)
The prevalence of being uninsured was estimated by occupational group and sociodemographic characteristics, stratified by year.
During 2014, 12.7% of workers aged 18–64 years were uninsured (21% decline from 2013)
The prevalence of being uninsured declined more (23%) in states that expanded Medicaid than in those that did not (9%; p = 0.013)
adjusted prevalences were estimated using logistic regression
CDC used data from the 2013 and 2014 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS)
the prevalence of being uninsured declined significantly (21%) from 16.0% in 2013 to 12.7% in 2014

methods_quotes.q: Data were weighted and analyzed to account for the complex BRFSS sampling design.
Unadjusted prevalences by occupational group were calculated to present the magnitude of noncoverage
adjusted prevalences were estimated using logistic regression
The initial model included occupational group, year, the interaction between occupational group and year
Weighted estimates adjusted by age group, sex, race/ethnicity, language in which the survey was administered
Estimates have a relative standard error >30% and ≤50% and should be used with caution
